meeting_header:
Date: 2027-04-06 | Time: 09:00 PT | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Reed (Redwood Solutions), Tom Hargreaves (CTO, Moraine), Linda Gomez (Network Eng), Samir Khan (InfoSec), Jae Park (SRE), Elena Ruiz (Cloud Ops)
summary: Intro discovery for Moraine Systems' private/VPC deployment. Focus: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, egress IP controls, regional gating for EU data, KMS/HSM integration, and pilot sizing. Action items and a follow-up deep-dive assigned.
topics: Data residency and regional restrictions (EU vs US)
Pilot scope — Dedicated capacity vs Hosted with private network
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're excited to chat through Moraine's private deployment needs. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Tom Hargreaves: Tom here, CTO.
[00:12] Linda Gomez: Linda, networks.
[00:14] Samir Khan: Samir, security.
[00:16] Jae Park: Jae, SRE.
[00:18] Elena Ruiz: Elena, cloud ops.
[00:20] Alex Morgan: Great, Priya and Daniel from my side. Priya will run the infra questions, Daniel can cover pilot/benchmarks.
[00:28] Priya Patel: Hey all. To start, can you give us the high level of how you want Redwood to sit in your VPC? Are you thinking peering, private endpoints, or a transit model?
[00:40] Tom Hargreaves: We're leaning private endpoints — we want no internet egress for inference traffic. But we're unsure about cross-region calls; some services run in eu-west and some in us-east.
[00:52] Linda Gomez: Yeah also our infra uses a central transit-gateway and we have multiple accounts. We need to understand whether Redwood can accept peering from our TGW or if we need PrivateLink in each account.
[01:10] Priya Patel: Right, so short answer: Redwood supports VPC peering and PrivateLink-style private endpoints. We also do transit-gateway attachments for enterprise Private deployments, but there are tradeoffs: peering gives simpler routing, PrivateLink gives stronger isolation and easier account boundary enforcement.
[01:30] Linda Gomez: How do you handle SNAT/egress? We need stable egress IPs for our downstream partners to whitelist.
[01:38] Daniel Reed: We can provide static egress IP ranges for Private/Dedicated placements — typically we allocate a block per customer region. There is a small NAT hop if traffic leaves the private plane for monitoring, but sensitive traffic can stay in customer-controlled path. Sometimes the transcript has a slight mis-hear: Daniel said "NAT hop" but text shows "NBAT hop" in notes.
[01:58] Samir Khan: On encryption — do you support BYOK via KMS or HSM? Our compliance team demands customer-managed keys.
[02:06] Priya Patel: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS. For PCI/PHI-tier customers we support HSM-backed CMKs and key wrap. We'll share the KMS integration docs — note sometimes in the auto notes it reads as "K M S hyphen" which is a transcription quirk.
[02:28] Tom Hargreaves: Also data residency. EU model instances have to keep logs and payloads in eu-west. Can you pin model instances per region?
[02:36] Alex Morgan: Absolutely — Redwood Private can pin model shards and inference nodes to particular regions. We can set routing policies that route EU traffic to eu nodes; fallback to US is possible but you'd want to disable that to be GDPR-strict.
[02:52] Elena Ruiz: What's the latency delta if we pin to eu-west vs running a single central node? 
[02:58] Priya Patel: If you place inference in eu-west we expect token latency similar to running in region; cross-region adds RTT which could add 80-150ms depending on path. For your average conversational model that's measurable but often acceptable. We'll share a primer with numbers from similar customers.
[03:18] Jae Park: For peering, we need to know what prefix ranges you expect, and whether you support overlapping CIDRs.
[03:26] Priya Patel: We recommend non-overlapping CIDRs; if overlap exists we can use PrivateLink or NAT-based relays. We'll send an IP plan template.
[03:36] Linda Gomez: Transit gateway: can you attach to our TGW and accept propagated routes? Or do you require manual route entries?
[03:44] Daniel Reed: We support TGW attachments. Usually we request a small set of static routes to be propagated and prefer explicit route tables on our side for security. In practice that's documented in the TGW playbook we'll share.
[03:58] Samir Khan: About audit logs — retention, granularity? We need per-request tracing for 90 days and immutable audit trails for admin actions.
[04:08] Priya Patel: Audit logs are configurable. For Private deployments we can stream logs to your S3 or your SIEM (via syslog/kinesis). Retention policy is configurable; note that cost for long retentions is separate. We'll include the retention matrix in the docs.
[04:26] Tom Hargreaves: Any cross-account IAM patterns we should model? We use SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning.
[04:34] Alex Morgan: Redwood Console supports SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM for provisioning. For Private installs we can integrate with your IdP and limit the admin plane to your network or IP range.
[04:48] |-- [04:50] (crosstalk) 
[04:52] Linda Gomez: Quick follow: do you provide egress IP slices by region? Our firewall vendor needs /28s not massive ranges.
[04:58] Daniel Reed: Yes, we can provide /28 blocks per region if needed; we'd coordinate with your firewall team.
[05:06] Priya Patel: Also want to flag quantization/CPU/GPU tradeoffs if you're thinking cost. Dedicated GPU pools reduce token cost and latency; hosted private endpoints with CPU-backed runtimes are cheaper but higher latency.
[05:20] Elena Ruiz: Our throughput target is 100 requests/sec with median request size of ~250 tokens. Does that push us to Dedicated?
[05:28] Daniel Reed: 100 rps with 250 tokens is fairly heavy; for predictable latency you'll want dedicated GPU pools. We recommend a pilot 2-node Dedicated with autoscale up to 6 nodes for burst. We'll size in detail after we see more telemetry.
[05:44] Samir Khan: What about fallbacks? If the private region goes down, do you have automatic routing to another region? We need graceful degradation policies.
[05:52] Priya Patel: Yes, we support canary and fallback policies. For strict residency you'd disable cross-region fallback. Otherwise we can route to a warm stand-by in another region with encrypted transit.
[06:08] Tom Hargreaves: Any vendor lock-in concerns? If we later want to move models or take models on-prem, how portable are the configs?
[06:16] Alex Morgan: We provide model versioning and exportable config manifests. For private deployments we can provide deployment artifacts that your infra team can run in an air-gapped mode, though some runtime license constraints may apply for specific models. We'll clarify per-model.
[06:34] Linda Gomez: Network nit: are you NATting traffic for metrics collection? We need to know whether observability hooks will traverse customer plane.
[06:42] Priya Patel: Observability hooks can be configured to send traces to customer endpoints in-region. There is an optional side-channel to Redwood console if you opt in — otherwise everything goes to your SIEM.
[06:56] Jae Park: For the pilot, can we run a smoke test with synthetic load and capture p95 latencies?
[07:02] Daniel Reed: Yes — we usually run a 2-week pilot: week 1 smoke/functional, week 2 load up to target traffic. We'll provide a benchmark script and sample payloads.
[07:14] Tom Hargreaves: Pricing: how does dedicated commit pricing compare to hosted with private endpoints?
[07:20] Alex Morgan: Dedicated has a reservation model — higher fixed commit, lower per-token cost. Hosted private endpoints are usage-based; you pay per-token plus a private endpoint surcharge. We can produce a TCO comparison for your expected volumes.
[07:34] Samir Khan: Any SOC2/ISO certs you can share now? We need to kick our procurement readout.
[07:40] Priya Patel: We'll share our SOC2 Type II and ISO excerpts, plus our third-party pen-test summary. Also provide a short KMS/HSM integration doc.
[07:52] Elena Ruiz: Regarding region gating: if we block US region, is there a way to verify traffic never leaves EU?
[07:58] Priya Patel: We can provide a signed network path attestation and logs showing node allocation and egress IP ranges; for strict compliance we recommend Private Dedicated in-region.
[08:12] Linda Gomez: A random note — does Redwood support BGP or are routes static?
[08:18] Daniel Reed: For TGW we accept dynamic propagation; for peering it's static routes. BGP sessions are an advanced option in some private deployments. We'll note that this is variable by cloud provider.
[08:34] Tom Hargreaves: Who will be our primary Redwood technical contact during the pilot?
[08:38] Alex Morgan: Priya will be the SE lead, and Daniel will assist on sizing and benchmarks. I'll coordinate timelines.
[08:46] [08:47] (short silence)
[08:52] Priya Patel: Okay I'm going to summarize action items: we'll send IP plan template, TGW playbook, KMS/HSM and SOC2 docs, pilot proposal with Dedicated sizing and cost comparison, and the benchmark script.
[09:06] Tom Hargreaves: That sounds good. We'll compile our egress whitelist and the TGW details and aim to send them by Friday.
[09:14] Alex Morgan: Great — next step: schedule a 90-minute deep-dive with your NetEng and our infra team for the TGW + peering specifics. Propose Tuesday 2027-04-12?
[09:26] Elena Ruiz: That works for us.
[09:28] Samir Khan: Also include a security deep-dive on 04-14 to review KMS and audit retention.
[09:34] Alex Morgan: Noted. Any other questions?
[09:36] Jae Park: One last — do you have any sample firewall rules for PrivateLink?
[09:40] Priya Patel: Yes we'll include sample SG/NACL rules and a sample iptables snippet for on-prem gateways.
[09:48] Tom Hargreaves: Great, thanks everyone.
[09:50] Alex Morgan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet.
[09:52] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-typed words (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache) and speaker overlaps. Some technical terms transcribed oddly (SOC Two, K M S).
